topics.label: 30. Canada: the product monograph and the label
33. Australia: PI, CMI and the black triangle
34. WHO prequalification: the SmPC of a WHOPAR

questions.q: Which symbol does a Canadian prescription drug label carry in the upper left quarter of the main panel?
questions.why: C.01.004(1)(a): "Pr"; no other drug may show it.

questions.q: How many digits does a Canadian DIN have?
questions.why: The drug identification number is eight digits, shown with "DIN".

questions.q: How large must the proper name be on a Canadian label?
options: The same size as the brand
At least half the size of the brand name
At least two sizes larger than the brand

questions.q: How long do entries stay in Recent Major Label Changes?
questions.why: The template says retain for 24 months.

questions.q: Where is the Serious Warnings and Precautions box?
questions.why: Section 3, with cross-references to the detailed sections.

questions.q: Which toll-free number does the Overdose box of the Canadian Patient Medication Information give?
questions.why: Health Canada's poison control number; 1-866-234-2345 is for reporting side effects to Canada Vigilance.
questions.cite: PM master template, Patient Medication Information

questions.q: In which date form is the date of authorization given on the title page?
questions.why: The template uses YYYY-MM-DD.

questions.q: In which annex of the AMZV is the Fachinformation set out?
questions.why: Annex 4; the patient information is Annex 5.1.

questions.q: Which products carry the Swiss black triangle?
options: New active substances, new biologicals, time-limited authorisations and authorisations with conditions
questions.why: AMZV Art. 14a.

questions.q: How long does a Swiss medicine stay under additional monitoring?
options: As a rule until the authorisation is renewed
questions.why: Until renewal, unless Swissmedic extends it.

questions.q: How is the Swiss authorisation number written?
questions.why: Five digits followed by "(Swissmedic)".

questions.q: Where does the Fachinformation give the dispensing category?
questions.why: The packs section gives the Abgabekategorie.

questions.q: Through which portal does the Fachinformation ask professionals to report?
questions.why: ElViS; ElViS 2.0 is planned for December 2026.

questions.q: A Japanese insert has no section 12. What number does OVERDOSAGE keep?
options: It is renumbered at the next revision
questions.why: Numbers are not moved up.

questions.q: What must a contraindication other than hypersensitivity include?
options: Its reason, briefly, in square brackets
questions.why: The rationale goes in [ ].

questions.q: When is section 1 WARNINGS used?
options: When fatal or extremely serious, irreversible adverse reactions can occur
questions.why: When alert is particularly needed.

questions.q: What do Japanese drug Standard Commodity Classification Numbers start with?
questions.why: Drugs are in class 87.

questions.q: Since when are paper inserts abolished in principle for prescription drugs?
questions.why: The electronic insert system took effect on 1 August 2021.

questions.q: How does a user reach the electronic insert?
options: By reading the code on the outer box with an app
questions.why: A barcode or 2D code on the outer box.

questions.q: How does the Australian PI title line start?
questions.why: The approved form sets it.

questions.q: Which number does section 4.9 give?
questions.why: The PI form text points to the Poisons Information Centre.

questions.q: How long does a medicine stay in the Australian black triangle scheme?
questions.why: Five years from first supply or approval of the new indication.

questions.q: What does the CMI start with?
options: A boxed warning in every case
questions.why: The CMI summary, required for prescription medicines.

questions.q: Which section of the PI gives the Poisons Standard schedule?
questions.why: Section 7 Medicine schedule (Poisons Standard).

questions.q: Which order sets the label standard for Australian prescription medicines?
questions.why: TGO 91; TGO 92 covers non-prescription medicines.

questions.q: Which part of a WHOPAR is the SmPC?
questions.why: Part 4 is the information for the health care provider.

questions.q: What does section 8 of a WHO PQ SmPC give?
questions.why: For example MA999(a).

questions.q: Are trade names prequalified by WHO?
questions.why: Trade names are the national regulator’s responsibility.

questions.q: What does the opening statement of the SmPC say?
options: It covers the uses prequalified by WHO; national authorities may authorise others
It is legally binding in every country
It is a summary for patients
questions.why: It sets the scope.

questions.q: Which frequency word belongs in section 4.8?
questions.why: The MedDRA convention.

questions.q: Which storage wording does the section guidance offer for 6.4?
questions.why: Standard optional wording.

questions.q: Which toll-free number does Reporting side effects give in the Canadian PMI?
questions.why: 1-844-764-7669 is the poison control number in the Overdose box.
questions.cite: PM master template, Patient Medication Information

questions.q: In which languages are Swiss texts published?
questions.why: The official languages; English translations are not binding.

questions.q: How does the Swiss patient information end?
options: With the month it was last checked by Swissmedic
questions.why: "Diese Packungsbeilage wurde im ... letztmals durch die Arzneimittelbehörde (Swissmedic) geprüft."

questions.q: How many numbered sections does the 2019-format Japanese insert have?
questions.why: From 1 WARNINGS to 26 MARKETING AUTHORIZATION HOLDER, etc.

questions.q: What comes before section 1 of the insert?
options: The header items, starting with the date of preparation or revision
questions.why: Header items A to G precede the numbered sections.

questions.q: Which section of the full CMI covers side effects?
questions.why: "Are there any side effects?" is section 6.

questions.q: Where does the PI point to www.tga.gov.au/reporting-problems?
questions.why: 4.9 gives the Poisons Information Centre number.

questions.q: Which section of a WHO PQ SmPC names the supplier?
questions.why: 8 is the WHO reference number, 9 the date of prequalification.

questions.q: What does section 9 give?
questions.why: Section 10 is the date of revision of the text.
